gaps.sentence: They said nothing at all, ___ I found rather strange.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' here means 'and this'; it refers to the whole situation and follows a comma.

gaps.sentence: Tell me ___ you said to her.
gaps.explanation: 'What you said' means 'the words that you said'; 'that' cannot head the clause after 'me'.

gaps.sentence: It was the first time ___ I had ever driven on my own.
gaps.hint: after 'the first time', use this pronoun
gaps.explanation: 'The first time that ...' is the standard pattern; the pronoun may also be omitted, but 'which' and 'what' do not fit.

gaps.sentence: The house ___ windows were broken has now been sold.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose windows' — the windows belong to the house.

gaps.sentence: The programme ___ I watched last night was about volcanoes.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to things, even when it is the object of the clause.

gaps.sentence: My uncle, ___ lives in Canada, is coming to stay next week.
gaps.hint: non-defining clause after a comma about a person
gaps.explanation: In non-defining clauses (between commas) 'that' is not allowed; 'who' refers to people.
'Who's' is the contraction of 'who is'; 'whose' shows possession and cannot stand before an adjective alone.

gaps.sentence: The person to ___ I addressed the letter has moved house.
gaps.hint: after a preposition, the object form for people
gaps.explanation: After a preposition the object pronoun 'whom' is required for people; 'that' and 'who' cannot follow a preposition.
